course_title: Psychology of Sport, Physical Activity and Health

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how psychological variables influence participation and performance in sport and exercise settings.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of how participation in sport and exercise influences the psychological characteristics of the individual player/participant.
Demonstrate applied knowledge about sport and exercise psychology as a practitioner (e.g., scientist, coach, HPE teacher, fitness instructor, athlete and/or exerciser).
Retrieve and critically review information relevant to topics of research in sport and exercise psychology.
Experience a general introduction to the research process in sport and exercise psychology through learning how to critique the literature.
Work effectively within a team in order to develop communication and process management skills, and facilitate peer-assisted, collaborative learning.

assessments.task_description:
Objectives

  • Demonstrate understanding of key concepts, theories, and evidence introduced throughout the course.
  • Encourage regular engagement with lectures, readings, podcasts, and workshops.
  • Consolidate learning across each module before progressing to the next.


Description

Students will complete four online quizzes throughout the semester, each covering the content from a major course module. Although completed online, the quizzes will be undertaken during the scheduled in-person workshop sessions (Weeks 4, 7, 11, and 13), and attendance at these workshops is therefore required. Quiz questions will assess students' understanding of concepts presented in lectures, required readings, podcasts, and workshop activities.

To pass this assessment, students will be required to demonstrate detailed comprehension of their submission independent of AI and MT tools.

assessments.task_description:
Objectives

  • Apply psychological theories of motivation to an authentic personal experience.
  • Critically reflect on the dynamic interactions between the individual, the task, and the environment.
  • Develop evidence-informed strategies to support ongoing motivation and behaviour change.
  • Integrate theory, research, and lived experience through creative communication.


Description

Working in teams of four to five students, each group will identify a shared sport, physical activity, or health-related goal to pursue over an eight-week period (Weeks 4–11). Midway through this journey (end of Week 8), each student will individually submit a Creative Motivation Timeline illustrating their own motivational journey.

The timeline will be organised around three phases—past, present, and future. Students will creatively represent where they were at the beginning of the journey, where they are midway through, and where they hope to be by the end of the project. Throughout each phase, students will reflect on themselves, the task, and their environment, drawing on psychological theories and concepts studied in class to explain how these interacting factors have shaped their motivation over time.

Rather than presenting motivation as something fixed, students are encouraged to illustrate its dynamic and evolving nature. They should identify key moments, challenges, turning points, and adaptations that influenced their journey, critically evaluating the strategies that have supported or hindered their progress. Building on these reflections, students will develop an evidence-informed action plan for the second half of the project.

The submission should take the form of a creative artefact that visually communicates the complexity of their motivational journey while integrating psychological theory and research. Students are encouraged to use timelines, diagrams, illustrations, photographs, symbols, or other creative approaches that best represent their experience.

The emphasis of this assessment is on thoughtful integration rather than description. Students are expected to critically connect course concepts to their own experiences, demonstrating how psychological theory can help explain, interpret, and improve real-world behaviour.


Use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT)

These tasks have been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. Whilst students may use AI and/or MT technologies, successful completion of assessment in this course will require students to critically engage in specific contexts and tasks for which artificial intelligence will provide only limited support and guidance.

A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct.

To pass this assessment, students will be required to demonstrate detailed comprehension of their written submissions independent of AI and MT tools.

assessments.task_description:
Objectives

  • Apply psychological theories and concepts to an authentic sport, physical activity, or health experience.
  • Integrate knowledge from motivation, cognition, emotion, and social processes to understand behaviour from multiple psychological perspectives.
  • Develop collaborative problem-solving, critical reflection, and evidence-informed practice.
  • Communicate learning creatively through a multimodal portfolio.


Description

Working in small groups, students will identify a shared sport, physical activity, or health-related goal and pursue it over an eight-week period (Weeks 4–11). Throughout their journey, students will document their experiences using a range of evidence and multimodal representations, such as photographs, videos, reflections, observations, performance data, creative artefacts, or other forms of documentation that best capture their learning and experiences.

The portfolio will be organised around the four core themes of the course—motivation, cognition, emotion, and social processes. For each section, students will critically reflect on their experiences by integrating relevant psychological theories and concepts explored throughout the semester. Students will be encouraged to compare different theoretical perspectives, including mainstream and transactional approaches, and evaluate how each contributes to understanding behaviour, performance, participation, and wellbeing.

The final portfolio will be presented as a digital artefact (e.g., PowerPoint, Canva, or another approved digital platform) that creatively communicates the group's journey while demonstrating the application of psychological theory to authentic, lived experiences. The emphasis of this assessment is not simply on achieving the goal itself, but on thoughtfully documenting, analysing, and reflecting on the psychological processes that emerged throughout the journey.

learning_activities.topic:
Introduction: Why Theory Matters – Four Ways of Understanding Sport, Exercise, and Health Behaviour

Online lecture: This week introduces the course and explores four major metatheoretical perspectives that shape how we understand behaviour in sport, physical activity, and health. Students will discover how different theoretical lenses lead to different research questions, interventions, and professional practices, providing the conceptual foundation for the rest of the course.

In-Person Workshop – Experiencing Theory Through the Body

In this first interactive workshop, students will engage in embodied, collaborative, and multimodal learning activities designed to experience the main theoretical perspectives of this course rather than simply learn about them. Through movement, discussion, and creative problem-solving, students will begin developing the systems thinking that underpins the course.



Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L06

learning_activities.topic:
Understanding Motivation and Goal Setting

Online lectures: This week examines why people participate and persist in sport and physical activity through major theories of motivation. Students will explore evidence-based goal-setting strategies and consider how goals can be used to support motivation, performance, and wellbeing.


Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04, L05

learning_activities.topic:
Motivation from a Transactional Perspective

Online Lecture: The goal of week 3 is to introduce motivation as something that emerges through the ongoing interaction between individuals and their environments. Students will explore how affordances and learning environments can shape motivation, engagement, and lifelong participation in physical activity.


Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04, L05

learning_activities.topic:
Workshop: Solving the Motivation Challenge

In-Person Workshop: This embodied and interactive workshop challenges students to address one of the biggest questions in sport, exercise, and health psychology: How do we help people move towards more active and healthier lifestyles? Through collaborative, multimodal problem-solving activities, students will apply motivational theories to design creative, evidence-informed solutions for real-world behavioural challenges.


Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L06

learning_activities.topic:
Cognition in Sport and Physical Activity

Online Lectures: This week explores the reciprocal relationship between cognition, physical activity, and sport. Students will first examine how physical activity influences executive functions and cognitive development before exploring how athletes perceive information, allocate attention, make decisions, and develop expertise in dynamic sporting environments. Contemporary approaches to perceptual-cognitive training and emerging technologies will be critically evaluated, encouraging students to consider not only their potential benefits but also whether improvements meaningfully transfer to performance.


Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04, L05

learning_activities.topic:
Decision Making: A Transactional Perspective

Online Lecture: This week introduces an ecological dynamics perspective on decision making, challenging traditional views of cognition as an internal process. Students will explore how decisions emerge through continuous interactions between the individual, the task, and the environment, and consider how practice environments can be designed to support adaptive behaviour.


Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04, L05

learning_activities.topic:
Workshop: Designing Enriched Environments for Cognition

In-Person Workshop: This practical workshop takes place in the gym, where students will experience how movement can be intentionally designed to stimulate cognition and support whole-person development. Through embodied experimentation, students will learn how to create enriched physical activity environments that promote attention, adaptability, creativity, and decision making.


Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L06

learning_activities.topic:
Understanding Emotion in Sport and Physical Activity

Online Lecture: This week introduces major theories of emotion and examines on one hand, how emotions influence performance, participation, and wellbeing, and on the other hand, physical activity and sport participation influence emotional states. Students will explore practical strategies for recognising and using emotions effectively in sport and physical activity.


Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04, L05

learning_activities.topic:
Adaptation from a Transactional Perspective

Online lecture: The goal of this week is to explore emotion as a dynamic process emerging through interactions between the individual and their environment. Students will examine how appropriately designed challenges can foster adaptive emotional states and resilience in sport and physical activity, including contemporary transactional approaches to psychological adaptation.

Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04, L05

learning_activities.topic:
Social Relationships in Sport and Physical Activity

Online Lecture: This week explores how relationships with coaches, teammates, parents, peers, and other social agents shape development, performance, and mental health. Students will examine the importance of creating supportive, psychologically safe, and developmentally appropriate sport and physical activity environments.

Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04, L05

Workshop: Emotion as an Embodied and Transactional Process

In-Person Workshop: This embodied workshop concludes the emotion module by inviting students to discover how emotions are experienced, expressed, and regulated through the body and movement. Through interactive and reflective activities, students will learn to design physical activity experiences that embrace a truly holistic understanding of human functioning.
